note: Every fixture the multivariate goldens reference. csv_md5 pins the committed CSV; the .pulse twin is written from it by internal/tools/refcohorts.

cases.name: attitude
cases.citation: Chatterjee, S. & Price, B. (1977) Regression Analysis by Example. New York: Wiley.
cases.note: 30 x 7 as shipped with R; w_freq / w_prob are SEEDED weights appended by the generator, not part of the data.

cases.name: mtcars
cases.citation: Henderson, H. V. & Velleman, P. F. (1981) Building multiple regression models interactively. Biometrics 37, 391-411.
cases.note: 32 x 11 as shipped with R (row names dropped); w_freq / w_prob are SEEDED weights appended by the generator, not part of the data.

cases.name: likert_ties
cases.note: six 1-5 Likert items on one latent factor; heavy ties for rank methods and alpha.

cases.name: nulls
cases.note: four correlated continuous fields, 6 nulls each at seeded rows: listwise and pairwise differ.

cases.name: weighted
cases.note: four predictors, a continuous / binary / count response, integer frequency weights and fractional probability weights, both with zero-weight rows.

cases.name: nonpsd_pairwise
cases.note: three blocks each observing one pair: r(x,y) ~ +1, r(y,z) ~ +1, r(x,z) ~ -1, so the pairwise Pearson matrix has a negative eigenvalue.

cases.name: heywood
cases.note: draws from a correlation matrix whose one-factor solution needs lambda_1^2 = .8*.8/.5 = 1.28 > 1: a Heywood case under minres.

cases.name: reversed_items
cases.note: five 1-5 Likert items, r2 and r4 reverse-keyed as stored (x' = 1 + 5 - x restores them).
